steps.message:
1. What exactly does the code at major_gc.c line 1274 do with the wosize it reads out of the first block of a run, and does it use that number to compute an address to jump to in the same way the sweep code does.

2. Is that number being interpreted as a count of separate blocks to be skipped or as a single size in word units, and are the two sides of the scheme actually in agreement on that point.

3. What meaning does the marking code attach to the first field of a block of this kind, in particular whether it will ever try to follow it as a pointer to other blocks.

4. Can you show the present form of the allocate and sweep changes since both are said to have been gone through and it is still not clear from the account what they each now write down.

5. Does the initialize part really place the first field in the condition the later code expects, or does it only set the count and leave that field to be filled in on some later occasion.

6. Is the build that dies being made as a debug runtime, since in that case the fields in question will have been overwritten with a special test marker.
steps.reasoning_content:
We need answer to user: they want me to begin by asking at least five questions about current state not answered in summary. We are on our own after asking. Need produce questions only? Likely final answer should be list of questions. Need think through context. We have OCaml runtime modification to major heap run-length compression of free space. Crash in do_some marking at major_gc.c line 1274. Previous agent says run length compression keeps count of following blocks in wosize of first block and pointer to next run in first field. They tried merging runs carrying first field of merged run to end of first (like allocate part), didn't cure, left in. Next look at points run first put together: allocate and sweep both gone through; initialize appears in order.

Need ask useful diagnostic questions. We can't execute? We are to ask, then on our own. We need get info not in summary. Questions should be about: exact code in major_gc.c at line 1274, and how do_some interprets wosize, because maybe it expects different bit layout. What is the value of the next-run pointer when run is detected, and is it a valid free list head? Whether the run length count is stored in the same wosize bits as normal block sizes, or a separate field/reserved bits. How the allocate path updates count when it consumes part of a run, including whether it writes the count back. Whether the sweep path has a special case to recognize an existing run, and if so how it distinguishes it from a normal free block. What the initial heap setup does to the first field of the first free block in each pool. Whether the build is a normal release or a debug build. The precise sequence of events before the crash, and whether it reproduces on a small test. Whether the count is ever decremented. The relationship between the stored count and the actual distance to the next run, since a mismatch would make the mark stack step over blocks. Also whether the pointer in the first field is to the next run or to the next block in a linked free list. And whether the first field is also used to carry block sizes for other purposes.

We need maybe formulate as direct questions to prior agent or to the code. The prompt says ask about current state of solution not answered. We can ask what the code at that line actually does. We can ask for the text of the modified allocate and sweep functions. We can ask how the header of a block is interpreted on the marking side. We can ask if the first field of the first block is ever used to hold a normal pointer that marking would dereference. We can ask whether the count was meant to be the number of block sizes or the total word size. We can ask if the pools are laid out so that the next run is immediately after the covered blocks.

Need maybe not too many. At least five. Since after that we are on our own, the questions have to be answerable from the repository. I should make them so that a subsequent inspection of the files can answer them. The line number in major_gc is the most important one because the whole scheme depends on that side reading the same two words. It is also necessary to know whether the count is being treated as a size in word units or as a number of separate blocks. The first field of a block may have a completely different meaning to the marking code, in which case the plan would be defeated even though the free list were managed correctly. The answer to whether the initialize code really does what is claimed will have to come from a close reading of that code. Whether the build that fails is a debug one or a normal one matters because the debug build fills those fields with a special marker.
